rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Sequential read of all 14 chunks: every pronoun/demonstrative resolves within-chunk or against an earlier-named term of the same file. Closest calls, both clean: chunk 3 line 41 'the most skipped' (subject = /clear habit, same sentence) and chunk 8 line 79 'The other kind' (back-references chunk 7's 'durable problems...and loud problems' two-kind split, allowed same-file sequential build). No never-named, no vague-with-history, no stranded-by-rechunk referent found. Harm (reader loses the thread) absent.

grep for cross-file phrasing ('the opening lecture said', 'earlier module') over lines 1-120 returns nothing in body prose. No file is named by position anywhere; the two prose mentions of 'later in the training' (chunk 4, line 49) point forward to unnamed future content generically, not at a specific file by position, and are not a resolution requirement (nothing to resolve). Harm absent.

rules_evaluated.evidence: This is a supplementary reference page, not an exercise/lecture with a module beat set. No 'the X you did/saw/caught' construction appears anywhere in the body (checked all 14 chunks). Rule has nothing to apply to.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess-before-reveal demo instruction anywhere in the file. The one interactive beat (chunk 2, 'Put a number on it', lines 17-35) is a compute-and-observe prompt, not a guess/predict-then-reveal beat, so there is no reveal-ordering to check.

Every chunk carries a self-standing claim or content unit even in isolation: e.g. chunk 10 'One lever, two payoffs' (lines 91-93) states its own thesis sentence rather than leaning on a wait-state. No chunk is a single context-dependent bullet.

Checked all 13 `##` headers against their chunk body under the sequential read; each is a literally true summary (e.g. line 79 'Drivers of inefficient context: the loud ones' matches its body's 'The other kind is loud but shrinking', line 79-85). Closest call: line 95 'Now go clean your window' against a reflective/meta closer (lines 95-101) — content ends on 'time to compact, or start clean', which is the same imperative the header states, so it holds.

Grepped body for 'Not X. Not Y.' constructions, anaphora/epistrophe triples, self-grading superlatives, number+retraction pairs, abstraction-noun stacks, and empty-leg verb triplets across lines 1-120: none found. The one superlative-shaped phrase, line 41 'the cheapest quality upgrade there is, and the most skipped', grades a practice (/clear), not the training/exercise itself, so it is not the self-grading value-prop-leak sub-item (`check_writing.md §13` targets claims about the training's own usefulness). The dollar figures in chunk 2 (line ~33) are a computed comparison with method shown, not a number-then-retraction tic.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Grepped for surface(noun)/firing/compendium/forcing function/beat/mood/Connections across lines 1-120. Two near-misses, both cleared: line 43 'beat a vector index' is the ordinary verb sense (outperform), not dialect-noun. Line 83's header 'The tool and MCP surface' and body 'tool and MCP surface' use 'surface' in the standard engineering sense (API surface / attack surface — interface area consumed by tool descriptions), the sense the compendium explicitly carves out as ordinary engineering usage, not the repo-internal 'writing surface' content-authoring dialect this rule targets. No repo-internal vocabulary reaches the room.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Per prior run's finding: 'Subagent as a firewall.' (line 49) was shortened to the handle form and is confirmed present, within the 5-word handle cap. Chunks 3, 4, 7, 8, 9 each carry 1-3 bolded handles (e.g. **Start clean.**, **Pass paths, not paste.** on chunk 3; **Subagent as a firewall.**, **Route by complexity, not price.**, **Keep what you carry lean.** on chunk 4) — these are consolidation slides listing named checklist items, matching the rule's own carve-out ('a law/consolidation slide may carry one handle per law'), not the flat ≤1-per-slide budget meant for narrative slides. Chunk 6 ('The folklore') carries two bolded handles ('"Caching saves you 90 percent."' line 65 and '"Compaction is always lossy, so always hand off."' line 67) that exceed the 5-word handle cap — per the maintainer accept-note at line 123 ('Future judges should score §9 N/A on that section rather than propose a trim'), these are quoted folklore claims under examination, not decorative handles, and per the preamble an accept-note on a passage is not re-flagged. Scored N/A-by-accept-note for that specific pair, folded into this PASS row per the completeness contract (one entry per rule).
